judged_text: The backfill INSERT interpolates raw setting values into SQL verbatim, bypassing EmbeddableHost's before_validation normalization (scheme/path stripping) and its format validation, so entries like 'https://example.com/1234' — explicitly supported by the old setting semantics and exercised by the specs this diff deletes — are stored with scheme and path and can never match `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)` in EmbeddableHost.record_for_host; blank lines become empty-string junk rows and a value containing a quote breaks the INSERT statement itself. Even once the cmd_tuples guard is fixed, sites whose admins entered hosts as URLs silently lose embeddability for those hosts immediately after upgrade, and a quote in the setting value aborts the migration mid-deploy.

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the backfill does `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`, directly interpolating the old `site_settings` string into SQL and bypassing `EmbeddableHost`'s `before_validation` normalization (scheme/path stripping) and its format validation (app/models/embeddable_host.rb). If an admin previously entered values like `https://example.com/1234` (explicitly shown as a supported input in the updated specs via Fabricate with that host), the migration will persist that full string; later, `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)` (host-only), which will not match a DB row containing scheme/path, breaking embeddability after upgrade. The raw SQL interpolation also means a value containing a quote would break/abort the migration, and empty lines can produce empty-string rows because the migration does no presence filtering before inserting.
